projects.title: Dude, Where's My Board?
projects.description: A San Diego surfboard aggregator that scrapes local shops, shaper sites, and marketplaces into a normalized catalog for browsing new and used boards in one place. Built with a Next.js frontend, Python scrapers, Supabase, and LLM-assisted normalization to power search, filters, and inventory freshness.
projects.summary: A searchable surfboard catalog combining local shops, shapers, and marketplaces.
projects.problem: Surfboard listings are spread across shop websites, shapers, and marketplaces, each with different formats and search options.
projects.approach: I built Python scrapers to collect listings, normalized the catalog with LLM-assisted processing, and connected Supabase to a Next.js frontend for search and filtering.
projects.result: The site brings new and used boards into one browsing experience, with filters and inventory freshness as core product features.

projects.title: TideEye: Underwater Visibility
projects.description: Vis is a full-stack computer vision application that analyzes live underwater camera footage from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography pier in La Jolla, CA to estimate horizontal visibility in real-time using a Beer-Lambert exponential attenuation model fitted across known-distance pier pylons. The system is deployed on a serverless AWS architecture (Lambda, S3, CloudFront, DynamoDB) with a React frontend, automated CI/CD via GitHub Actions, and integrates live oceanographic data from CDIP buoy stations and Open-Meteo to provide divers and researchers with continuously updated visibility forecasts.
projects.summary: Computer vision applied to underwater visibility at the Scripps pier.
projects.problem: A live underwater camera shows conditions, but a useful visibility estimate requires relating the image to known distances and ocean conditions.
projects.approach: I built a computer vision pipeline that fits a Beer–Lambert attenuation model across known-distance pier pylons. A serverless AWS backend feeds a React frontend alongside CDIP buoy and Open-Meteo data.
projects.result: TideEye presents camera-derived visibility estimates alongside oceanographic context. The estimate is model-based and depends on what can be measured in the camera image.

projects.title: World Cup Tracker
projects.description: A World Cup prediction-pool tracker that replaces manual spreadsheet scoring with a repeatable Python pipeline and a static React frontend. It syncs tournament standings, scores each entrant's group and knockout picks, generates leaderboard snapshots as JSON, and presents live leaderboard, bracket, and third-place race views in a mobile-friendly UI.
projects.summary: Automated prediction-pool scoring with leaderboard and bracket views.
projects.problem: Manually scoring tournament prediction pools in spreadsheets makes standings and bracket updates repetitive.
projects.approach: I built a Python pipeline to sync standings, score group and knockout picks, and generate JSON leaderboard snapshots for a static React frontend.
projects.result: Entrants can browse the leaderboard, bracket, and third-place race through one mobile-friendly interface.

projects.title: My Personal Site
projects.description: The site you are on now! Built from the ground up with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and hosted on GitHub Pages with Cloudflare as the CDN. Automated deployments via GitHub Actions on every push to main.

projects.title: WMATA DC Metro Analysis
projects.description: Developed a Websocket off the WMATA API, run in an AWS instance alongside a Javascript-based webpage for live train and bus locations. Lambda functions utilized in tandem with main site to feed route information, timings, and predicted arrivals.

projects.title: Hype Words: Social Media Mining and Classification
projects.description: Utilized web scraping techniques to curate live datasets of social media posts, then exploring classification techniques to understand social media sentiment around Blockchain in Healthcare. Successfully applied a transformer-based approach to text classification using BERT.

projects.title: Visualizing Bird Migrations
projects.description: Processing of geojson, csv, and netcdf files to showcase Swainson Hawk migration patterns.

projects.title: NOAA: Waves and Buoys Scraping
projects.description: Utilize Beautiful Soup to crawl NOAA API endpoints for Buoy and Wave data to then store and visualize on a web-page map via Javascript.

projects.title: Regularization Techniques
projects.description: An exploration of regularization techniques from Ridge to LASSO to SCAD, on Forest Fires, Boston Housing, and randomly generated datasets.

projects.title: Comparing Regressors
projects.description: Analysis of various regression approaches from localized kernel-based regression (LOWESS) to neural networks in their efficacy on predicting Boston Housing Prices.

projects.title: Music Frequency Analysis
projects.description: A frequency exploration of songs from 1791, 1976, and 2021. Spectrographic analysis is done to see the differences between these three eras and genres.

projects.title: El Nino/La Nina Time Series Analysis
projects.description: An exploration of how the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) can have public health implications globally, with analysis done using spectral density, periodograms, and autocorrelation function plots.
